target_customer: Brick-and-mortar retail chains (fashion, sports, telecom, grocery) that already have CCTV cameras
problem: Physical retailers lack the analytics online stores have. Aura Vision turns existing security camera feeds into footfall, dwell, queue and conversion metrics.
business_model: B2B SaaS per store or camera with an edge device

founders.name: Daniel Martinho-Corbishley
education: PhD in Computer Vision and Machine Learning, University of Southampton
founders.background_notes: Company about page names Daniel and Jaime as founders with PhDs at Southampton; YC page lists Daniel Martinho-Corbishley.

founders.name: Jaime Lomeli-Rodriguez
education: PhD in Computer Vision and Machine Learning, University of Southampton
founders.background_notes: Per YC page and company about page.

founders.name: Jonathon Blok
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder on the YC page only; the company about page does not mention him.

investors: University of Southampton Web Science Institute Z21 Innovation Fund

technical_complexity.rationale: Accurate people counting and demographic estimation from low-quality CCTV on a cheap edge device within a 50 Kb/s per camera budget needed deep learning research expertise, which the PhD founders had.

defensibility.rationale: Algorithms were copyable by well-funded vision vendors, but camera and POS integrations and enterprise rollouts across hundreds of stores add some lock-in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Aura Vision remains independent and serves Virgin Media O2, Flannels, Decathlon and Adidas UAE per its site.

market_need_then: A 2019 industry study cited by Automate found only 3 percent of merchandisers used computer vision while 40 percent planned to, showing latent demand for in-store analytics.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain and practical: Instant answers. Faster decisions. Computer vision AI, without the hassle.

branding.brand_signature: Ask Aura, a natural language assistant for store questions

brand_strength.rationale: Competent B2B brand with case studies and trade show presence, but the name is shared with a spiritual aura scanner app and other products and shows no community pull.

outcome_analysis: Aura Vision grew out of University of Southampton PhD research, took a small grant in 2018, raised about $1.1M in June 2019 after YC and has since landed enterprise retail chains including Virgin Media O2 (307 stores). It remains independent with about 10 staff. Funding appears modest relative to retail analytics rivals, so traction rests on enterprise rollouts and capital efficiency rather than large rounds.
notes: Funding conflict: the company's about page says a $2.1M seed after YC; Bouncewatch lists $2.15M; the company's earlier release said $1.1M. Recorded $1.1M (trade press) and treat higher totals as unverified. The 2018 grant was reported in GBP (100,000 pounds) by Southampton and another source says 141,000 dollars; amount left null. CB Insights lists a Seed II in June 2021 with Wayra UK, unverified. The seed blog URL returned 404. Competition list empty: the one dated search (retail computer vision 2018 to 2019) named no specific rivals and I did not find a dated source naming them; Jonathon Blok appears on the YC page only.
